bull_bear.body:
- Integrated manufacturing ecosystem spanning design studio, advanced EVA injection-moulding, rotary-type PU injection and 5th-generation sports-shoe machinery, supporting a portfolio of 1,500+ active SKUs
- Extensive pan-India distribution network (27 states, 520+ distributors) combined with a growing export footprint (20+ countries)
- OEM partnerships with established consumer brands (Spykar, Red Chief, Cult Sport, Lee Cooper) validating manufacturing quality and providing capacity-utilisation upside
- Diversified revenue base across own-brand footwear (Lehar, Rannr), OEM manufacturing and an asset-light government toolkit-supply business
- Three decades of manufacturing experience with a track record of technology adoption (Italian EVA machinery, automated PU pouring, rotary PU injection)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competitive intensity in the footwear industry — Management flags that organised domestic manufacturers, international brands and regional players compete across multiple product categories and price segments, pressuring market share and pricing.
- Changing consumer preferences and fashion cycles — Evolving fashion trends and rising expectations on quality, comfort and design require the Company to respond with agility through continuous product innovation and design refreshes to stay relevant.
- Talent attraction and retention — Management identifies attracting and retaining skilled employees as essential to sustaining operational excellence and long-term growth, addressed via compensation and engagement initiatives.
- Cybersecurity and information-systems risk — Increasing integration of digital technologies into operations makes safeguarding information systems and business data a key priority; the Company has implemented cybersecurity and information-security measures to mitigate this.
- Export demand subdued by geopolitical and tariff uncertainty — Exports remained subdued during FY2025-26 due to the challenging geopolitical environment and tariff-related uncertainties affecting global trade, a structural risk to the Company's export growth strategy.
- Dependence on a government scheme for the toolkit business — The toolkit business operates under the Government of India's PM Vishwakarma Scheme; continuity and scale-up of this revenue stream depend on the scheme's execution framework and government programme continuity, though management is working to expand beyond carpenter toolkits into additional trades.
- Execution risk on the new Kundli athleisure manufacturing facility — The dedicated athleisure manufacturing facility at Kundli, Sonipat is expected to commence commercial operations only in Q2 FY2026-27; delays in commissioning or ramp-up could affect the Company's growth plans in the athleisure segment.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Lehar Footwears Limited manufactures non-leather footwear across sports shoes, athleisure, sandals, slippers, clogs and school shoes under its Lehar brand and its newly launched sports/athleisure brand Rannr, alongside a growing OEM manufacturing business supplying leading domestic brands. The Company also operates an asset-light toolkit-supply business, having been awarded a ₹298 crore agreement with NSIC under the Government's PM Vishwakarma Scheme in 2024. Products are sold pan-India through a distributor network and exported to over 20 countries.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Footwear (own brand - Lehar):** Sports shoes, Athleisure, Casual shoes, Slippers & sandals (formal & casual), Kids shoes (casual, school & canvas), EVA footwear, Clogs
- **Footwear (own brand - Rannr):** Sports and athleisure footwear (closed footwear segment, launched 2025)
- **OEM manufacturing:** Sports and athleisure footwear supplied to third-party brands including Spykar, Red Chief, Cult Sport and Lee Cooper
- **Toolkit supply:** Toolkit supplies under the Government's PM Vishwakarma Scheme, in partnership with NSIC

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Premiumisation: expand presence in sports footwear and fashion-led categories, enhance product design and introduce more premium offerings to improve average selling prices and product mix.
- OEM manufacturing: strengthen partnerships with leading domestic and global brands, leveraging the integrated manufacturing platform to raise capacity utilisation and diversify revenue streams.
- Market expansion: deepen the pan-India distribution network and broaden presence across large-format stores, modern trade and e-commerce platforms.
- Export growth: deepen presence across 20+ countries, supported by the diversified product portfolio and manufacturing capabilities, to diversify revenue geographically.
- Build a balanced manufacturing model in which the platform supports the Lehar and Rannr consumer brands while also serving reputed third-party OEM customers.
- Scale the toolkit-supply business from a single trade to multiple trades within the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, based on proven execution and early-mover credibility.
- The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs. 0.50 per equity share (5.00%) for FY2025-26, consistent with a final dividend of Rs. 0.50 paid for FY2024-25, subject to a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (per Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations) available on the Company's website. No amount was transferred to the General Reserve during the year, and the Company reported no unclaimed dividend older than seven years requiring transfer to the Investor Education and Protection Fund.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY2025-26 the Company undertook a significant capacity expansion by establishing a new manufacturing facility at Kundli, Haryana, aimed at enhancing production capabilities, improving operational efficiencies and strengthening market presence. The Kundli facility is being scaled in a phased manner from approximately 1 lakh sports-shoe pairs per month towards 5 lakh pairs per month, with the first phase (to 2 lakh pairs/month) expected to commence from Q2 FY2026-27; the location was chosen for its access to North Indian markets and major logistics hubs. Alongside the new facility, the Company installed fully automated EVA injection-moulding machinery and rotary-type PU injection machinery as part of its premiumisation strategy and expansion into sports and athleisure footwear, and commenced manufacturing of sports shoes under its new in-house brand 'Rannr', marking its entry into the closed footwear segment. Historically, the Company's manufacturing footprint grew through the 2003 introduction of imported Italian EVA machinery in Rajasthan, the 2013 acquisition of the Kaladera manufacturing facility (~14,770 sq. metres) and its 2015 commissioning for expanded production. The Company's strategic manufacturing facilities are located at Jaipur and Kundli, together forming part of a stated 5-facility manufacturing footprint.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising disposable incomes, rapid urbanisation and improving employment levels are strengthening discretionary consumer spending on footwear and more frequent replacement purchases.
- Consumers are gradually shifting from unbranded to branded footwear, favouring quality, design, comfort and durability, supporting higher value realisation for organised manufacturers such as the Company.
- Athleisure has emerged as one of the fastest-growing footwear categories, driven by health consciousness and casual dressing trends, supporting the Company's entry into closed footwear via Rannr.
- GST rationalisation (footwear priced up to Rs 2,500 reduced from 12% to 5%) is expected to improve affordability, stimulate demand and strengthen the competitiveness of organised manufacturers.
- Expanding Tier II/III and rural markets, aided by improving rural incomes and retail penetration, are creating demand opportunities beyond metropolitan cities for value and affordable footwear.
- India's low per-capita footwear consumption (~2 pairs versus a global average of 7-8 pairs) is cited as significant long-term headroom for demand growth.
- Global supply-chain diversification under China+1 sourcing strategies, together with India's expanding FTA network (India-UK CETA, India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, India-EFTA TEPA), is expected to improve India's footwear export competitiveness and create sourcing opportunities for domestic manufacturers.
- Continued formalisation of the Indian footwear industry - shift from the unorganised sector towards organised, compliant manufacturers, aided by GST compliance, BIS standards and e-commerce expansion - favours established players.
- Domestic demand-led growth (FY2025-26 real GDP growth of 7.7%) and steady urban/rural consumption are cited as a supportive operating backdrop for consumer-facing manufacturers.
- Subsequent to the close of FY2025-26, the Company secured its largest-ever OEM footwear order (~18 lakh pairs), which management says strengthens revenue visibility for FY2026-27.
- The Union Budget for FY2026-27 proposes a Rs 3,861 crore outlay for the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, the government programme under which the Company's toolkit-supply (NSIC) business operates, cited by management as an early-mover advantage and credibility as a key vendor.
